children.name: Joinvillea ascendens Gaudich. ex Brongn. & Gris
children.description: Joinvillea ascendens Gaudich. ex Brongn. & Gris — a robust, rhizomatous perennial herb with strongly plicate leaves and hollow stems, growing up to 5 m tall in wet forest understories and along streams from sea level to 1920 m elevation. Native to the Hawaiian Islands, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Micronesia, New Caledonia, and Samoa. The Hawaiian subspecies is a candidate for Endangered Species Act listing with fewer than 200 individuals remaining, threatened by feral pigs, invasive species, and fungal pathogens. Flowers are small, perfect, and borne in large terminal panicles; fruits are fleshy drupes dispersed by birds.

children.name: Joinvillea bryanii Christoph.
children.description: Joinvillea bryanii Christoph. — a compact, tufted grass-like herb endemic to Samoa, with stems rarely exceeding 2 m and densely clustered, strongly plicate leaves. Type collected by L. W. Bryan on Tutuila in 1930. Often treated as a synonym of J. plicata (as J. plicata subsp. bryanii). Inhabits wet forest understories; flowers are small, perfect, trimerous, borne in terminal panicles; fruits are fleshy drupes.

children.name: Joinvillea borneensis
children.description: Joinvillea borneensis Becc. — a large grass-like herb with pleated leaves and fleshy drupes, native to western Malesia (Borneo, Malay Peninsula, Philippines, Sumatra) east to the Caroline Islands. Typically found in disturbed forest, forest edges, and on ridges at 620–2800 m elevation. Described by Odoardo Beccari from specimens collected in Borneo in 1878. Sometimes treated as J. ascendens subsp. borneensis. The inflorescence is a much-branched terminal panicle of small trimerous flowers; pollination may involve bees, and fruits are bird-dispersed.
